name: Benjamin Harrison
role: US president (1889-1893) and senator from Indiana (1881-1887)
summary: A Republican who governed as a high-tariff protectionist, backing the McKinley Tariff, reciprocity deals, ship subsidies and a larger navy. He urged federal protection of black voters' ballots, civil service merit rules, railroad safety laws and curbs on trusts, favored exclusion of Chinese and other immigrants, and moved toward overseas expansion with the Hawaii treaty.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: Said friendly arbitration in proper cases should be adequate for peaceful adjustment of all international difficulties.

ban-cartels.rationale: Asked Congress in 1889 to consider restraining trusts formed to monopolize necessities and the first federal antitrust law came in his term.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Described the American policy as avoiding all interference in European affairs.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Called for equal civil and political rights for black citizens but signed on to exclusion of Chinese immigrants; a mixed record.

free-trade.rationale: His administration enacted the McKinley Tariff, the highest protective tariff in US history up to then, instead of freer trade.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: His administration reduced the large reservations by allotment in severalty and opened surplus land to settlement.

military-superiority.rationale: Pressed for building modern warships so the navy would not face unequal combat.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: Backed bimetallism and the 1890 act issuing Treasury notes against silver bullion, wanting every dollar equal in value to gold and silver coin.

office-by-exam.rationale: Extended the classified civil service, enforced the merit law and put promotions on a record of merit.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: Urged that Utah be governed so that believers in polygamy could not make it lawful and praised the repressive legislation of Congress.

patriotic-education.rationale: Welcomed the renewed interest of schoolchildren in the national flag as a hopeful sign for future citizenship.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Wrote that the country must exclude alien races whose assimilation is neither possible nor desirable and called the case against Chinese immigration conclusive.

racial-franchise.rationale: Called for a free ballot for the workingman without distinction of race, and said limits on suffrage must be found in the law only.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Called for stricter naturalization and exclusion of paupers and contract laborers while saying the country should not cease to be hospitable to immigration; mixed.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Asked Congress in four messages to require railroads to fit automatic couplers and brakes, and in 1889 asked whether federal law could restrain trusts that crush competition.

separate-church-state.rationale: Gave hearty approval to the platform declaration on liberty of conscience and the separation of church and state.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Backed subsidies to build US ocean steamship lines and, with the 1890 tariff, bounties and duties to start tin plate and similar industries.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Defended protective tariffs as the wage barrier against European labor and made the 1890 tariff a central achievement; his acceptance letter endorses the American doctrine of protection.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Submitted a treaty annexing Hawaii to the Senate in February 1893.

women-suffrage.rationale: As senator voted against amendments stripping women's suffrage from Washington Territory's law but did not vote on the 1887 amendment; no later statement.

notes: Read in full or by theme: the inaugural, four annual messages, the 1892 acceptance speech, the Hawaii message and the 1888 campaign speeches, plus Senate roll calls. Themes searched: tariff and trade, trusts, labor and railroad safety, money, immigration and Chinese exclusion, Indians, polygamy and religion, civil service, elections and race, women, temperance, navy and foreign policy, Hawaii. Not available locally: his Senate speeches beyond a few, his post-presidential books, and the Geary Act text (not cited). He had no recorded position on most statements (health care, wages, unions, taxes on wealth, guns, abortion, family, courts), so those are null.
